The 10 Most Sacred Days of the Year Are Here — Are You Ready?

What the Prophet ﷺ did differently in Dhul Hijjah — and the simple daily plan every Muslim (not just hajji) needs right now

By Nazia Firdous  ·  June 3, 2026  ·  10 min read

Author: Nazia Firdous — Founder, Sabr And Sukoon | Islamic Wellness & Faith-Based Healing  ·  Published: June 3, 2026  ·  Reading Time: 10 min

💡 Content Integrity: All Quranic ayaat and ahadith in this article are sourced from authenticated collections (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Ibn Majah, Sunan Abu Dawud). Scholarly references cross-verified for accuracy.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said something that should stop us in our tracks every single year — yet most of us let these days pass like any other.

"There are no days on which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days."

— Sahih al-Bukhari

The Companions asked: "Not even jihad in the way of Allah?" He ﷺ said: "Not even jihad — except for a man who goes out risking his life and wealth and comes back with nothing."

Not even jihad. Let that land for a moment.

The first ten days of Dhul Hijjah are the most spiritually charged days in the Islamic calendar. Allah ﷻ Himself swears by them in the Quran. The Prophet ﷺ intensified his worship during them. And yet — most of us, especially those not performing Hajj — let them pass without intention, without preparation, without even noticing. This article is your reminder. These days are here. Right now. And they belong to you too.

Why These Days Are Extraordinary — Allah Swears By Them

In the Quran, Allah swears an oath by very few things. The sun. The night. The soul. And these days:

"By the dawn. And by the ten nights."
— Surah Al-Fajr, 89:1-2

Classical scholars of tafsir — including Ibn Abbas, Ibn Kathir, and the majority — identified "the ten nights" as the first ten nights of Dhul Hijjah. When Allah swears by something in His Book, it is a sign of its immense significance. He is drawing our attention. He is saying: pay attention to this window.

What Makes These 10 Days Different From All Others?

Scholars explain that these days carry extraordinary spiritual weight because they combine the greatest acts of worship simultaneously — Hajj, Qurbani, fasting (especially Arafah), takbeer, dhikr, Salah, sadaqah, and tawbah — in a way no other period in the year does.

1

The Best Days — By Divine Declaration

The Prophet ﷺ called them the greatest days of the year. Not Ramadan's last ten nights — those are the best nights. These are the best days. Both together cover the full spectrum of sacred time in the Islamic year.

2

Day of Arafah — The Crown Jewel

The 9th of Dhul Hijjah is the Day of Arafah — the greatest single day in the Islamic year. The Prophet ﷺ said fasting on this day expiates the sins of two years: the year before and the year after. One day. Two years of forgiveness. This alone should make us run toward these days.

3

All Pillars of Islam Converge Here

Salah, Sawm (fasting on Arafah), Zakat/Sadaqah, and Hajj all intersect in these ten days. It is the only time in the year where every form of major worship is active simultaneously. The doors of reward are open in every direction.

What the Prophet ﷺ Did Differently in These Days

Sayyidah Hafsah رضي الله عنها narrated that the Prophet ﷺ never abandoned four practices:

"Fasting the ten days of Dhul Hijjah, the three days of each month (Ayyam al-Beed), two rak'ahs before Fajr, and Witr."

— Sunan Abu Dawud & Sunan al-Nasa'i

He ﷺ also intensified his dhikr during these days. The takbeer — Allahu Akbar — would fill the days and nights from the 1st to the 13th of Dhul Hijjah. The Companions would say it loudly in the markets, in the masjid, everywhere — until the spirit of glorification permeated the entire community.

Your Simple Daily Action Plan — For Non-Hajjis

You do not need to be in Makkah to maximize these days. Here is what you can do — starting today:

🤲

Fasting (Days 1–9)

Fast as many of the first nine days as you can. At minimum, fast on Day 9 — the Day of Arafah. The Prophet ﷺ said it expiates two full years of sins. If fasting all nine is difficult, even three or five days carries immense reward.

📿

Takbeer — Say It Out Loud

Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, wa lillahil hamd. Say this walking, cooking, driving, before sleep. This is the Sunnah of these days — and it is so simple that most people overlook it entirely.

📖

Quran — A Daily Portion

Commit to at least one page — or one surah — each day. The deed is small. The reward, in these days, is multiplied beyond measure. Even Surah Al-Ikhlas three times equals the reward of reciting the entire Quran — imagine that in these blessed days.

💛

Sadaqah — Give Something Every Day

It does not need to be large. Feed a person. Give someone water. Pay a bill for someone struggling. The Prophet ﷺ said sadaqah does not decrease wealth — and in these days, its reward is at its peak. Ten days, ten acts of giving.

🌙

Tawbah — Sincere Repentance

These days are a gift of mercy. Use them to return. The Prophet ﷺ would make tawbah 70 to 100 times every single day — and he was sinless. How much more do we need it? Make tawbah each morning and night. Allah loves those who turn back to Him.

✨

Tahajjud — Even Two Rak'ahs

Wake before Fajr — even just once in these ten days — and stand before Allah in the quiet of the night. He descends to the lowest heaven and asks: "Is there anyone seeking forgiveness so I may forgive them?" In Dhul Hijjah, this question echoes with special urgency.

⭐ The Crown of These Days

Day 9 — Arafah: The Greatest Day of the Year

Even if you fast no other day — fast this one. The Prophet ﷺ said fasting on the Day of Arafah expiates the sins of the previous year and the coming year. (Sahih Muslim)

On this day, millions of pilgrims stand on the plain of Arafah making du'a. And you — wherever you are — can join that spiritual gathering from your own prayer mat. Make your longest du'a of the year on this day. Ask for everything.

"The best du'a is the du'a on the Day of Arafah." — Sunan al-Tirmidhi

The Psychology of Sacred Windows — Why Intention Matters Now

Behavioral psychology tells us that time-bounded goals dramatically increase follow-through. We are more motivated, more focused, and more consistent when we know a window is closing. Islam understood this 1,400 years ago — and built sacred seasons into the year for exactly this reason.

💡 Faith-Science Insight

Research on "temporal motivation theory" shows that the perceived value of a goal increases as its deadline approaches. Dhul Hijjah is Allah's built-in deadline — a 10-day window where the value of every deed is at its highest. Setting a clear niyyah (intention) at the start of Day 1 measurably increases the likelihood of consistent worship throughout.

🤲 Du'a for These Blessed Days

اللَّهُمَّ بَلِّغْنَا رَمَضَانَ

"Allahumma ballighna Ramadan" — O Allah, let us reach and benefit from these blessed days

And: "Allahumma a'innee 'ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni 'ibadatik"
O Allah, help me remember You, be grateful to You, and worship You in the best manner.

Frequently Asked Questions — Dhul Hijjah 2026

When do the first 10 days of Dhul Hijjah 2026 start?

The first 10 days of Dhul Hijjah 2026 begin on approximately June 27, 2026 (subject to moon sighting). The Day of Arafah falls on Day 9, and Eid ul-Adha is on Day 10. Check your local Islamic authority for confirmed dates.

What are the best deeds to do in the first 10 days of Dhul Hijjah?

The Prophet ﷺ specifically recommended fasting (especially Day 9 — Arafah), abundant takbeer and dhikr, recitation of Quran, sadaqah, tawbah, and extra Salah including Tahajjud. Any righteous deed — however small — carries its greatest possible reward during these days.

Is fasting all 10 days of Dhul Hijjah compulsory?

No — fasting the first nine days of Dhul Hijjah is a highly recommended Sunnah, not obligatory (fard). However, fasting on the Day of Arafah (Day 9) is so strongly encouraged that no Muslim who is able should miss it. Note: Fasting on Day 10 (Eid ul-Adha) is haram — it is forbidden to fast on Eid.

Can I benefit from Dhul Hijjah if I am not performing Hajj?

Absolutely — and this is one of the most beautiful gifts of these days. The Prophet ﷺ did not limit the reward to those performing Hajj. Every Muslim worldwide can maximize these days through fasting, dhikr, Quran, sadaqah, and tawbah. You are spiritually connected to the ummah gathered at Arafah even from your home.

What is the Takbeer of Dhul Hijjah?

Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, wa lillahil hamd. This is the Takbeer al-Muttlaq — it is said from the 1st of Dhul Hijjah onwards. The Takbeer al-Muqayyad (after each fard salah) begins from Fajr of the Day of Arafah until Asr of the 13th of Dhul Hijjah.

Are the first 10 days of Dhul Hijjah better than the last 10 nights of Ramadan?

Scholars differ on this. Ibn Taymiyyah رحمه الله held that the days of Dhul Hijjah are the best days of the year, while the nights of Ramadan (especially Laylat al-Qadr) are the best nights. So: the 10 days of Dhul Hijjah are superior by day; the last 10 nights of Ramadan are superior by night.

"These ten days are not a gift only for those in Makkah.
They are Allah's gift to every heart that turns toward Him."

— Sabr And Sukoon

May Allah allow us to reach these blessed days, worship in them with sincerity, and have our duas answered. Ameen. 🤲
